title: Review of c08's NRCH crystal-ramp negative: replicated on seed 2 (24 swimmers, 0 persistent splits, occupancy 0.27); a steeper ramp to phi_t=-0.15 also ends as a lattice of 24 fatter swimmers, after a transient band phase
summary: Verdict written before reading other reviews. I ran c08's world.py unchanged (ramp -0.4 -> -0.3 over t=3000-8000) with labkit on new seed 2 to t=9000 (192^2, 1000 steps per frame as in the finding), and a steeper arm on the same seed (ramp to -0.15 over t=3000-6000). Default ramp: the lattice holds 24 swimmers at the end (mean 23.6), 21 tracks alive >= 50% of the run, 6 splits and 0 persistent, occupancy 0.27, up to 92 body lengths travelled. Steep ramp: at t~4700 swimmers elongate into wavy bands that break up again by t~5500 into a lattice of 24 larger swimmers (occupancy 0.36, persistent-track area ratio 4.35); labkit counts 3 persistent splits and generation 2, all from band break-up during t~4700-5500, not from single swimmers dividing.

observations.finding: rerun/seed2/FACTS.md: final 24 components, 0 persistent splits, occupancy 0.27; rerun_steep/seed2/sheet.png t=5950-9050: the same count (24) of fatter swimmers after the ramp to -0.15

seeds_run.result: pass (steeper ramp to -0.15; transient bands, number unchanged at the end)

controls_run.finding: steeper ramp arm rerun_steep/seed2 (phi_t to -0.15 over t=3000-6000)

verdicts.limitation: One new seed per arm. The steeper ramp shows a size limit exists: past it swimmers merge into bands instead of dividing, and the bands then re-fragment into a lattice with about the same number of bodies, so the lattice spacing (not the feed) seems to fix the count; I did not vary the box size to test that.
